MCF Sunday snapshot (11-22)

New here? See previous posts for the basics (setups, R, the accounts).

The pile (image 1):

  • Our setup generator screened about 27,000 machine-made rule ideas. We logged 1,136 research ideas and built 274 setups. 228 have traded live.
  • Today: 208 running across 10 paper accounts. 54 of them are in the Graveyard (still trading, just for data), and 12 are retired.
  • 36 are in the green, and about 15 show real promise. Only 4 make Primary.

Leaderboard (image 3): our top 10 right now. Ones marked * are machine-made. The top two have only 7-8 days of history, so we're excited but patient.

Busiest money-makers (image 2):

  • Gap-Down Recovery Fade: a stock opens way down and bounces, and we bet the bounce fades. +64R over 4 weeks.
  • Gap-Down Early Bounce Short: same idea, earlier and pickier. +60R, but bumpier.

Hot streaks:

  • Late Quiet-Day Short (shorts weak stocks late on days the Nasdaq is down): 5 green days in a row.
  • PM Upper-Wick Short and Late-Morning New-High Short: 4 each.
  • Lunch New-Low Short: 3.
  • We see streaks like this all the time, and most cool off. Midday Stretched Dip Buy looked great, then gave back 28R in 5 days. A setup needs weeks, not a streak, to get promoted.

Fun what-if: if Primary had only ever run its three gap-down shorts, it would be +77R on 550 trades. Everything else it ran: −207R. Gap-Down Recovery Fade alone in Primary: 188 trades, 67% winners, +36R.

Glitches we fixed:

  • Broker close-out glitch (11-05/06): a position didn't close and showed a fake $11.5k paper loss. Positions are now checked every minute, and closing retries until it works.
  • Runaway bursts: one setup fired 100 trades in minutes on 11-20 (−99R). A burst brake starts Monday.
  • Sleepy safety check: our outage watchdog wasn't actually running. It's now started by the trading jobs themselves.

Quick facts:

  • Paper money only.
  • Every number is after costs. A cost bug fixed this week made the older numbers look worse, but honest.
  • Promotion = a move up, not a copy.
  • The Graveyard never deletes.

Thanks as always!
